title: ODRL Offer
description:
CDIF Access profile of an ODRL 2.2 Offer (https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/#policy-offer): the baseline access and usage conditions a data provider sets for a digital object, without naming who they apply to (that is an ODRL Agreement). Built on the generic odrlPolicy block, which carries the ODRL structure; this block adds only CDIF's own rules. Draft from the CDIF Access spreadsheet (CDIF_Access_Profile_ODRL_Classes_Properties_Description.xlsx) and the cdifbook data_access chapter.
Keys carry the odrl: prefix and the document's @context declares the odrl, cdifa1 (https://w3id.org/cdif/access/profile1/), rdf and xsd prefixes. The ODRL JSON-LD context is not used, so nothing coerces a string to an IRI: every IRI value (target, action, parties, operands) is an {"@id": ...} object.
An access condition (something done BEFORE the digital object is retrieved) is a permission duty constrained by odrl:event odrl:lt odrl:policyUsage (https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/#duty-perm). Everything else is a usage condition: a permission (may do), an obligation (must do) or a prohibition (must not do).
OPEN QUESTIONS are marked "OPEN:" below.

@context.description: JSON-LD namespace prefixes for ODRL policy properties. Not required: an Offer embedded in a CDIF record inherits the record's @context.

@id.description: Globally unique, resolvable IRI for this Offer (the spreadsheet's uid). A resolver should be able to return application/ld+json, not only an HTML page.

odrl:profile.description: The CDIF Access ODRL profile this policy uses, which supplies the cdifa1: actions the ODRL core vocabulary lacks (download, assent, datadestruction, ...). OPEN: nothing is published at this IRI yet, and it names a .ttl file where ODRL expects a profile identifier. The cdifa1: form is accepted because compaction under the cdifa1 prefix rewrites the full IRI to it.

odrl:target.description: Asset all rules apply to, if given once at policy level (range odrl:Asset).

odrl:assigner.description: The party issuing the Offer, normally the repository or data custodian, given once at policy level (range odrl:Party). ODRL also accepts an assigner on every rule instead; CDIF asks for the policy-level form. The spreadsheet does not list an assigner yet.

odrl:assignee.description: Party all rules apply to, if given once at policy level (range odrl:Party).

odrl:permission.description: Actions a user may perform on the target (usage conditions).

odrl:target.description: The asset, normally a distribution or data service (range odrl:Asset).

odrl:output.description: An asset created by exercising the action (range odrl:Asset).

odrl:action.description: The permitted action (range odrl:Action). OPEN: the cdifa1 action vocabulary is not defined, so values are not enumerated; whether it is an ODRL profile or a standalone controlled vocabulary is still to be settled.

odrl:assigner.description: Party granting this permission, if not given at policy level (range odrl:Party).

odrl:assignee.description: Who may exercise the permission (range odrl:Party), as a party or a (refined) PartyCollection, e.g. registered users located in the UK. This is the book's form; the spreadsheet scopes users with odrl:constraint instead. OPEN: settle on one, or say when each is used.

odrl:constraint.description: Conditions on exercising the permission (range odrl:Constraint), e.g. only users located in the UK (the spreadsheet's way of scoping users; see odrl:assignee).

odrl:duty.description: Access conditions (range odrl:Duty): actions that must be completed before the permitted action, e.g. assent to an End User Licence before download.

odrl:obligation.description: Actions every user of the target must perform (range odrl:Duty), e.g. destroy the data at the end of a project. The spreadsheet gives 1..*; drafted as 0..* because an Offer with only permissions is common. OPEN: confirm.

odrl:prohibition.description: Actions a user must not perform (range odrl:Prohibition), e.g. share TRE credentials.

odrl:output.description: An asset created by exercising the action (range odrl:Asset).

odrl:assigner.description: Party issuing this prohibition, if not given at policy level (range odrl:Party).

odrl:assignee.description: Who the prohibition applies to (range odrl:Party).

odrl:constraint.description: Conditions under which the prohibition applies (range odrl:Constraint).

odrl:remedy.description: Duties owed if the prohibition is infringed (range odrl:Duty).

accessConditionMarker.description: The constraint odrl:event odrl:lt odrl:policyUsage: the duty must be fulfilled before the permission is exercised. In CDIF Access this is what marks a duty as an access condition. Each operand accepts the odrl: compact IRI and the full IRI.

AccessCondition.description: A permission duty carrying the accessConditionMarker. The spreadsheet gives the duty action as 1..*; ODRL allows one action per rule, so several pre-conditions are several duties. OPEN: the spreadsheet does not say what an assent duty assents to (e.g. which licence document); a duty target is one candidate. OPEN: the spreadsheet lists constraint @type with cardinality 1 but gives no value and omits it on this constraint, so it is optional.

odrl:action.description: The action to complete first, e.g. cdifa1:assent (range odrl:Action).
